C1. The age sweep (2026-07-07) REJECTED age 5/6/7 on the SAFETY gates only - net rose +7.5% at age 5 (+288 trades) but worst trade went -983 -> -1246 and combine pass 97.7% -> 95.9%. What that sweep never varied was SIZING: run_age_sweep.py mutates only FVG_MAX_AGE_BARS and inherits RISK_BUDGET_SIZING_ENABLED intact, so an age-5 entry was sized from the same per-score budget map ({8:900,7:675,6:350}) as a fresh age-1 entry. Under risk-budget sizing a -1246 loss on a <=900 budgeted stop IS the gap-through overshoot, and it scales linearly with size - so halving the budget on aged entries should scale the worst case with it (~ -623) while keeping most of the added frequency. Requires a new OFF-by-default flag pair (FVG_AGED_ENTRY_RISK_MULT + FVG_AGED_ENTRY_MIN_AGE=5) tested with FVG_MAX_AGE_BARS=5. Grid is {0.50, 0.35} and NOTHING MORE: if 0.50 fails the tail gate, do not walk the grid hunting a passing value - that is the tuning failure mode TDC/SPC were killed for. Pass requires ALL of: worst trade <= -983 (baseline, not merely better than -1246), combine pass >= 96.7%, net >= 95% of baseline in every split, and trade count strictly above baseline. BLOCKED FOR THE GENERIC RUNNER ON PURPOSE: this candidate is a PAIR of parameters (FVG_MAX_AGE_BARS=5 AND FVG_AGED_ENTRY_RISK_MULT). nightly_researcher.py sets exactly one attribute, so running it here would leave the age gate at 4, admit no aged entries at all, and record a no-op as a clean 'no change' verdict - a misleading result in the ledger. Run research/run_aged_entry_sizing.py instead (same imported decide() rules, plus the trade-count gate). The inert flags are already in src/bot.py (FVG_AGED_ENTRY_RISK_MULT=1.0 default = byte-identical live behavior).

C2a. At 29.6% WR the book is a few large winners and a losing day is the common case, while the combine needs 5 qualifying days >= $150 plus a $3k target without a -$1,000 breach. Taking partial profit at the wired defaults (40 ticks, 60% of size) converts trades that reach +40 ticks and then round-trip into small GREEN days - a direct attack on the qualifying-day-count and daily-limit-fail gates, requiring no additional trades, which is the right shape given the supply-decay study shows supply is the binding constraint. Expected to cost net; the gauntlet decides whether it buys pass-rate faster than it sells net (net gate loosened to 90%, tail gate unchanged at -983). WARNING - do not treat a SHIP here as a config flip: topstepx_runtime.py submits a single full-size bracket and manages only the stop, with no scale-out path (see the ~1-exit-fill assumption at line 1169), so shipping C2a requires new live order-management code plus test_risk_and_safety.py coverage on BOTH the backtest and live signal paths. Sequenced after trail_after_mfe_on for that reason.

C2c. Third of the three never-tested exit-side flags. Kills trades that have sat 24 bars without prior-bar MFE reaching 8 ticks, freeing the single-position slot. Lowest prior of the three: with supply already scarce (1.2 trades/day, 31.8% zero-trade sessions) the position slot is rarely the binding resource, so the mechanism it targets may not bind. Run it last, single-flag, standard gauntlet, same combine-first judging as C2a/C2b. Do not combine with the other exit flags until at least one has cleared on its own.
